summary: Scheduler-to-runtime handoff 504 on broad token budgets during long-context priming
description: Issue summary: Customer Quill Analytics reports repeated 504 HTTP timeouts when sending priming requests with very wide max_tokens budgets (40k-80k) and large multi-document system prompts. Impact: Customers experience aborted generations at finalization, causing downstream application failures and failed billing attempts for partially emitted tokens. Environment: Dedicated pool (pool-id dq-prod-9), prod/us-east-1, app-level client retries enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use Redwood API generate endpoint with max_tokens=60000 and a 12-document priming payload (~45k tokens priming). 2) Set streaming=true and client read deadline 120s. 3) Observe initial tokens emitted, then abrupt 504 returned around 70-95s. Observed behavior: Final chunks never arrive and connection resets with a 504 from the API gateway. Server-side traces show finalizer queue growth and a subsequent stall during a scheduler->runtime handoff where the runtime kernel rotation was triggered. Expected behavior: Long-context generations complete or degrade gracefully (fallback to smaller model / partial emit) without returning 504 for in-flight streams. Logs/Diagnostics: - Finalizer queue length spiked from typical 2-4 to 42 on the affected worker (worker-23). - Scheduler logs indicate handoff latency spikes to ~18s during the time of the event. - Runtime traces (trace IDs: trace-20260310-8a7b) show kernel rotation start followed by repeated preemption attempts and a stuck kernel swap future. - No OOM or GPU panic recorded. - Network metrics to client remained within baseline. Repro instructions: Run the above steps against pool dq-prod-9 with a customer token and collect traces with request header x-trace-id. Attach: excerpted runtime trace, scheduler timing histogram, and a short client curl sequence in comments.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: large priming loads push finalizer queue past a saturation threshold during rare kernel rotations. Correlated scheduler latency spikes with a concurrent maintenance window for driver-level firmware rollout on a subset of workers. Investigations so far: - Replayed customer payloads against a staging pool without the firmware changes: reproduces but with lower frequency. - Replayed payloads on affected prod workers with driver firmware version v2.14.1: consistently reproduces. - Patch PRs found referencing preemption logic in scheduler (see related_github_prs). - Memory timelines show KV cache growth but not eviction spikes prior to stall. - Observed that batching was enabled for these requests; large batch coalescing may exacerbate kernel rotation timing. Hypothesis refined: combination of aggressive batching + in-progress kernel rotation on a worker with new firmware causes the runtime to stall during the handoff, filling the finalizer queue and triggering gateway timeouts. Next steps: 1) Mitigate by disabling batching for requests with max_tokens > 30k for affected dedicated pools. 2) Reproduce on a controlled fleet segment with driver rollback to v2.13.x. 3) Instrument finer-grained kernel-swap metrics and add guardrails to preempt rotation if finalizer queue exceeds threshold.
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Nair (Support): Customer opened ticket after three 504s in one hour. Collected request IDs and an attached runtime trace. Initial triage assigned to Diego.

2026-03-10 Diego Patel (SRE): Reproduced behavior against dq-prod-9. Observed finalizer queue spike and scheduler handoff latency. Temporarily set customer-level batching disabled as a test; customer reported fewer failures but still saw slowdowns.

2026-03-11 Marco Alvarez (Runtime): Kernel rotation instrumentation shows a future not resolving when a preemption path was hit. This coincides with driver firmware rollout on ~15% of workers. Suggest rolling back firmware on those workers for further validation.

2026-03-11 Elena Morris (Solutions): Quill Analytics confirmed they were sending large multi-doc priming payloads as part of nightly sync. Requested a temporary rule that routes their traffic to a non-rotating worker subset.
2026-03-12 Diego Patel (SRE): Deployed a scheduler patch that adds a guardrail to avoid initiating kernel rotation when finalizer queue > 10. Observing production over next 48 hours.
2026-03-13 Quill Analytics (Customer): After guardrail and temporary batching disable, failures dropped from ~3/hour to 0 over 24h. Noted one delayed final chunk (120s) but no 504s.
2026-03-14 Marco Alvarez (Runtime): Prepared rollback plan for driver firmware on affected hosts and a follow-up runtime patch to abort rotations cleanly if preemption paths take longer than 8s.
2026-03-14 Diego Patel (SRE): Marking as In Progress while mitigation verified. Will update with PR and rollout schedule in next 24 hours.
resolution: Workaround implemented: - Scheduling guardrail preventing kernel rotations when finalizer queue > 10 deployed to prod (scheduler PR merged). - Customer-specific rule applied to Quill Analytics' dedicated pool to disable batching for requests with max_tokens > 30k. Outcome: immediate reduction in 504s. Next actions: - Rollback of driver firmware on affected hosts planned (change window scheduled 2026-03-16). - Runtime patch to add hard abort on rotation preemption path (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123) targeted for canary 2026-03-17. - Postmortem and runbook update assigned to Marco Alvarez. Follow-up: monitor Quill's error rate and finalizer queue metrics for one week; if stable, close ticket and document permanent fixes in Confluence.
